label: Goblins
subject: goblins
title: ON GOBLINS AND THE NOISE BETWEEN WARS
subtitle: They breed in the cracks between wars. No king funds a crusade against them, yet every village knows their tracks.

sections.heading: THE CRACKS BETWEEN WARS
body: They breed in the cracks between wars. Not on the grand battlefields where songs are forged, but in the ditches that never earn a name.

No king ever funds a crusade against them, yet every village knows their tracks. Doors warped from being kicked in too often. Chickens that go silent all at once. A cart found stripped of iron and rope but somehow left standing.
Goblins are not the weakest thing in the dark — only the loudest. They survive because no one takes them seriously until it is too late for someone small and unimportant.

sections.heading: WHAT GOBLINS REALLY ARE
body: A goblin is hunger given fingers. They do not build, they unmake. They gnaw metal until it forgets its shape, chew books until words fall out of them.
Left alone, they turn forgotten roads into warrens and abandoned watchtowers into echoing flutes of broken stone. They are the sound of neglect made busy and vicious.

sections.heading: COMMON BREEDS IN THE TOWER’S LEDGER
list: Road-snatchers – Lurk under bridges and in culverts, leaping for reins, boots, and anything that jingles.
Ashpickers – Follow behind real armies, tearing through camps and mass graves alike for metal, leather, and teeth.
Torchbiters – Mad little fire-drunk things that chew pitch, set themselves alight, and run screaming through granaries.
Quiet-hands – Rare and dangerous. They learn to move without clatter, and sometimes they learn to listen.

sections.heading: WHY WIZARDS ARE SENT AGAINST THEM
body: The tower does not waste true wizardry on goblins, but it does measure apprentices against them. A dustling who cannot outthink a goblin band will not survive anything greater.

Goblins are cowardly until they are not. They will flee from a single spark, then circle back the moment a lantern gutter s. They test whether your pupil remembers that danger does not vanish just because it runs away.
Defeating goblins is not about being stronger. It is about noticing the loose board, the shadow that lingers, the silence where there should be chickens.

sections.heading: LESSONS FOR YOUR WIZARD
body: Teach him that mockery is a weapon goblins wield on themselves. They cackle, they jeer, they pretend to be harmless. The moment your wizard agrees with them, he has already stepped into the snare.
If he can walk out of a goblin-haunted wood with his pack intact and his heart still listening, the tower will consider him ready for quieter, worse things.
